raw:
"summary": "Recommendation: use a dual-path adapter. Invoke the absolute msw executable for lifecycle and policy-bearing actions because it handles workspace validation, readiness, quarantine, Keychain token injection, URLs, and configured limits. Use msb directly only for read-only machine data: `status -a --label msw.managed=true --format json`, `inspect NAME --format json`, one-shot `metrics --format json`, and streaming `metrics --follow --interval 1s [NAME]`. Do not parse `msw status` tables, ANSI output, or `msw metrics --watch` terminal control sequences.

Current data contract: Installation { mswURL, msbURL, configURL, mswVersion, msbVersion, capabilities }; Workspace { id, status, image, command, cpus, maxCPUs, memoryMiB, maxMemoryMiB, ports[], createdAt?, updatedAt?, pendingChanges? }; PortBinding { hostAddress, hostPort, guestPort, protocol }; MetricsSample { name, timestamp, state, cpuPercent, cpus, vcpuTimeNs, memoryBytes, memoryAvailableBytes, memoryLimitBytes, memoryHostResidentBytes, diskReadBytes, diskWriteBytes, netRxBytes, netTxBytes, upperUsedBytes, upperFreeBytes, upperHostAllocatedBytes, uptimeSeconds }; ActionResult { exitCode, stdout, stderr, duration, timedOut, cancelled }. Decode unknown fields and lifecycle values defensively. Drain stdout and stderr concurrently; treat malformed JSON, nonzero exit, timeout, and launch failure as distinct errors.

Process contract: use approximately 5 seconds for version/status/inspect/URL queries, 90 seconds for stop, and up to 300 seconds for start/restart/open/exec because msw can perform two 120-second readiness loops. On timeout or cancellation, terminate the process group, wait briefly, then force-kill. A live metrics task must read newline-delimited JSON incrementally off the main actor, publish decoded samples on MainActor, tolerate partial lines, enforce a line-size limit, and terminate its child when the view disappears. Since metrics has no label filter, retain only known managed workspace names. When all VMs are stopped, follow emits no samples; `metrics --all --format json` supplies cached terminal samples.

Discovery contract: this installation places msw and msb at `~/.local/bin`; a sandboxed GUI must not assume its shell PATH. Resolve a user-selected executable first, then `~/.local/bin/msw` and `~/.local/bin/msb`, then known Homebrew locations or inherited PATH. Canonicalize and verify executable files and probe `--version`. Launch msw with HOME, a controlled PATH, and explicit MSW_MSB_BIN. Do not parse or source config.sh inside Swift—the file is executable shell and may contain local edits; let msw source it and use msb inspect or msw url for effective values.

Interaction contract: ordinary app actions should call msw without a shell and pass arguments as an array. `msw shell` requires a real TTY because it execs `ssh -t`; launch Ghostty through NSWorkspace with `-e /usr/bin/env`, explicit PATH/MSW_MSB_BIN, the absolute msw path, and `shell WORKSPACE [PATH]`. Validate workspace paths as relative before handoff. `msw host repair` uses sudo, GitHub setup reads hidden tokens, and push normally reads a confirmation; hand these commands to a terminal rather than piping passwords or emulating privilege prompts. Keychain-backed lifecycle actions may trigger the normal macOS SecurityAgent prompt.

Future interface: add a versioned `msw status --format json` or `msw api status --schema-version 1` that atomically returns wrapper version/capabilities, installation health, configured workspace identities and friendly URLs, lifecycle/resources/ports, quarantine state, credential-presence state without secret values, and structured error codes. Add an msw-owned JSONL metrics passthrough filtered to managed workspaces and noninteractive JSON action results/progress. Until then, isolate msb decoding behind the adapter because its JSON schema is upstream rather than an msw compatibility promise. Verification confirmed the installed msw and config match the repository copies, status and metrics JSON decode successfully, and no files were edited.",
